title: The lobster fiefs: Economic and ecological effects of territoriality in the Maine lobster industry
description: Informal territoriality ('harbor gangs'): fishermen defend perimeter-defended areas, cutting trap lines of intruders after warnings.
evidence: Defended areas have larger lobsters, higher catch and incomes.
pathology: Violence and exclusion of newcomers.

title: The Economics of Roscas and Intrahousehold Resource Allocation
description: Rotating savings and credit associations: members contribute each meeting and one receives the pot in rotation, with social sanctions for default.
evidence: ROSCA participation mostly by married women with independent income, used to protect savings from husbands' claims.

title: The Carrot or the Stick: Rewards, Punishments, and Cooperation
authors: Andreoni, J., Harbaugh, W. & Vesterlund, L.
field_of_use: lab proposer-responder game with reward/punish options
description: Responder may reward, punish, or both after proposer's offer.
evidence: Punishment alone and reward alone each modestly raise offers; combination most effective; rewards and punishment are complements.

title: Achieving Cooperation under Anarchy: Strategies and Institutions
description: Reciprocity strategies (tit-for-tat), lengthening the shadow of the future via issue-linkage and decomposition, and international regimes that aid monitoring.
evidence: Descriptive/comparative case analysis.

title: An Evolutionary Approach to Norms
description: Metanorms: punish those who fail to punish defectors.
evidence: Simulations: norms collapse without metanorms, established with them.

title: Provision of Public Goods: Fully Implementing the Core through Private Contributions
description: Provision point with money-back guarantee: contributions refunded if the threshold is not met.
evidence: Theory: undominated equilibria implement efficient provision.

title: Communication and Cooperation in Social Dilemmas: A Meta-Analytic Review
description: Pre-play communication (cheap talk) among dilemma participants, face-to-face versus written.
evidence: Large positive effect of communication on cooperation; face-to-face much stronger than written; larger groups weaken effect.

title: Reward, punishment, and cooperation: A meta-analysis
authors: Balliet, D., Mulder, L.B. & Van Lange, P.A.M.
description: Meta-analysis of incentive-based institutions (rewards and punishments) in social dilemmas.
evidence: Both rewards and punishments have moderate positive effects on cooperation; effects stronger when incentives are costly to administer and in iterated dilemmas.

title: Team Incentives: Evidence from a Firm Level Experiment
authors: Bandiera, O., Barankay, I. & Rasul, I.
venue: Journal of the European Economic Association
description: Rank incentives and team tournaments.
evidence: Stronger incentives lead workers to form teams by ability rather than friendship.
pathology: Rankings reduce productivity in some teams.

title: Self-Enforcing International Environmental Agreements
description: Self-enforcing treaties where signatories adjust abatement in response to membership; later work adds trade restrictions (Montreal Protocol).
evidence: Theoretical: self-enforcing agreements achieve much only when gains from cooperation are small.
pathology: Large-gain agreements are not self-enforcing (narrow membership).

title: Vaccination and the theory of games
description: Game-theoretic analysis showing voluntary vaccination is a public good subject to free-riding.
evidence: Theory: voluntary coverage below eradication level.
pathology: Free riding on herd immunity.

title: Crime and Punishment: An Economic Approach
description: Optimal enforcement trades off probability of apprehension and severity of fines to deter offenses at least social cost.
evidence: Theoretical: high fines with low detection probability can be efficient.

title: Local-level management and the commons problem: A comparative study of Turkish coastal fisheries
description: Rotational lottery of fishing spots: sites allocated annually by lot and fishers rotate daily through them.
evidence: Descriptive: rotation reduces conflict and equalizes access.

title: Opting out of the Legal System: Extralegal Contractual Relations in the Diamond Industry
description: Private arbitration with reputational sanctions: bourse members settle disputes internally and unpaid judgments are posted, leading to expulsion and industry-wide boycott.
evidence: Descriptive: extralegal system handles nearly all disputes more cheaply than courts.

title: Rotating Savings and Credit Associations, Credit Markets and Efficiency
authors: Besley, T., Coate, S. & Loury, G.
description: Random and bidding ROSCAs allocate the pot; social sanctions deter default by early recipients.
evidence: Theoretical welfare comparison with credit markets.
pathology: Default incentive after receiving the pot.

title: Group lending, repayment incentives and social collateral
description: Joint liability with social collateral: group members impose social penalties on defaulting members.
evidence: Theory: social sanctions improve repayment.
pathology: Joint liability can cause whole-group default.

title: Fines, Leniency, and Rewards in Antitrust
description: Compares antitrust fines, leniency for reporters, and cash rewards for whistleblowing cartel members.
evidence: Leniency strengthens deterrence; rewards drive prices to competitive level.
pathology: Fines alone raise surviving cartels' prices; leniency stabilizes surviving cartels; fines used as retaliation between members.

title: Communication and punishment in voluntary contribution experiments
authors: Bochet, O., Page, T. & Putterman, L.
field_of_use: lab VCM with chat room, numerical cheap talk, face-to-face, and punishment
description: Compares communication formats with and without peer punishment.
evidence: Chat-room and face-to-face communication raise contributions about as much as punishment; adding punishment to communication adds little.

title: Egalitarian Behavior and Reverse Dominance Hierarchy
description: Reverse dominance hierarchy: the group collectively uses ridicule, criticism, ostracism, and execution to curb would-be dominants.
evidence: Cross-cultural survey (descriptive).

title: Punishment and partner switching cause cooperative behaviour in a cleaning mutualism
field_of_use: cleaner wrasse and client reef fish
description: Clients respond to cleaner cheating (biting mucus) by chasing the cleaner (punishment) or switching partners.
evidence: Both punishment and partner switching reduce subsequent cheating.

title: Image scoring and cooperation in a cleaner fish mutualism
field_of_use: cleaner wrasse (Labroides dimidiatus) and client fish
description: Clients eavesdrop on cleaners' interactions and preferentially approach cleaners seen cooperating.
evidence: Cleaners behave more cooperatively when observed by bystanders.

title: Monetary incentives increase COVID-19 vaccinations
description: A modest cash payment (SEK 200) for getting vaccinated.
evidence: Payment increased vaccination rate by ~4 percentage points.

title: Promoting Compliance with Human Rights: The Performance of the United Nations' Universal Periodic Review and Treaty Bodies
description: Peer review of states by states (UPR) and expert treaty-body review generate pressure and learning.
evidence: Interviews: UPR perceived as generating stronger pressure (political, peer-based) while treaty bodies stronger on expertise.
pathology: Politicization of peer review.

title: Promises and Partnership
field_of_use: lab trust game with pre-play messages
description: Non-binding promises sent before a trust game; guilt aversion makes people live up to others' expectations.
evidence: Promises increase trust and trustworthiness.

title: On compliance
description: Managerial model: compliance achieved through transparency, reporting, capacity-building, and dispute resolution rather than coercive sanctions.
evidence: Descriptive: most states comply most of the time; noncompliance mainly from ambiguity and capacity.

title: Cooperation under the threat of expulsion in a public goods experiment
authors: Cinyabuguma, M., Page, T. & Putterman, L.
field_of_use: lab VCM with majority vote to expel members
description: Group can vote to expel members; expelled players lose access to the group's public good.
evidence: Expulsion threat raises contributions to near-full levels; few expulsions occur.

title: Punishment in animal societies
description: Retaliatory aggression that reduces the payoffs of cheating, parasitism, or failure to cooperate.
evidence: Review and models.

title: Why Arms Control Is So Rare
description: Monitoring/inspection must render arming transparent enough to assure compliance but not so transparent that it threatens security.
evidence: Evidence the transparency-security trade-off has undermined arms control historically.
pathology: Inspection intrusiveness reveals exploitable military information, blocking agreements.

title: Social Capital in the Creation of Human Capital
description: Network closure enables effective norms and sanctions, trustworthiness via obligations and expectations.
evidence: Empirical: closure associated with lower dropout rates.

title: A flexible assurance bonding system for improved environmental management
description: Environmental assurance bond: firms post a bond equal to worst-case damages, refunded as they demonstrate lower damage.
evidence: Proposal; descriptive/theoretical.
pathology: Capital cost may exclude smaller firms.

title: Can Catch Shares Prevent Fisheries Collapse?
authors: Costello, C., Gaines, S.D. & Lynham, J.
description: Catch shares (ITQs): rights-based individual quotas of total allowable catch.
evidence: Catch shares halt, and even reverse, the global trend toward collapse.

title: A Review of Design Principles for Community-based Natural Resource Management
authors: Cox, M., Arnold, G. & Villamayor Tomás, S.
description: Empirical evaluation of Ostrom's design principles, reformulated (e.g., splitting monitoring into user and resource monitoring).
evidence: Principles well supported empirically.

title: Institutions and Behavior: Experimental Evidence on the Effects of Democracy
authors: Dal Bó, P., Foster, A. & Putterman, L.
field_of_use: lab repeated PD with voted payoff modification
description: Subjects vote on whether to adopt a fine-like payoff modification that makes cooperation dominant; compared with random computer imposition.
evidence: The same policy raises cooperation more when chosen democratically than when exogenously imposed ('democracy premium').

title: The Struggle to Govern the Commons
authors: Dietz, T., Ostrom, E. & Stern, P.C.
description: Adaptive governance: providing information, dealing with conflict, inducing rule compliance, providing infrastructure, encouraging adaptation.
evidence: Review.

title: Is the good news about compliance good news about cooperation?
authors: Downs, G.W., Rocke, D.M. & Barsoom, P.N.
description: Enforcement school: high compliance reflects shallow agreements; deeper cooperation requires credible punishment.
evidence: Argument: selection effects make compliance rates uninformative about enforcement need.
pathology: Shallow treaties: compliance without real cooperation.

title: The Hidden Hand of Economic Coercion
description: Threat of economic sanctions to coerce concessions; most successes occur at the threat stage.
evidence: Data show many successful coercion episodes end with sanctions threatened but not imposed.
pathology: Imposed sanctions have low observed success (selection).

title: Who Blows the Whistle on Corporate Fraud?
authors: Dyck, A., Morse, A. & Zingales, L.
description: Whistleblowing by employees and other non-traditional actors; monetary rewards (qui tam) strengthen incentives to report.
evidence: Employees, media, and regulators detect much fraud; in healthcare, where qui tam rewards exist, employees blow the whistle far more often.
pathology: Whistleblowers suffer significant career costs.

title: A Simple Mechanism for the Efficient Provision of Public Goods: Experimental Evidence
description: Budget-balanced mechanism that taxes below-average contributions and subsidizes above-average ones.
evidence: Mechanism moves contributions close to the efficient Nash prediction.
code: transfer based on deviation from average

title: Signaling Foreign Policy Interests: Tying Hands versus Sinking Costs
description: Hand-tying (public commitments generating audience costs) versus sinking costs (costly mobilization) as credible signals.
evidence: Theoretical.

title: Cooperation and Punishment in Public Goods Experiments
description: Group members may pay to reduce the earnings of low contributors after seeing contributions; peer punishment is used even when costly and in stranger matching.
evidence: Contributions rise and are sustained near high levels with punishment versus decay to near zero without it.
pathology: Some punishment of high contributors; efficiency losses from punishment costs in early periods.

title: Altruistic punishment in humans
description: Altruistic punishment: costly sanctioning of free riders with no future interaction, driven by negative emotions toward defectors.
evidence: Cooperation flourishes with punishment and breaks down without it, even with perfect stranger matching.

title: Detrimental effects of sanctions on human altruism
field_of_use: lab trust game with optional sanction threat
description: Investor can threaten a fine if trustee back-transfer falls below a desired level.
evidence: Using the sanction threat reduced back-transfers; forgoing an available sanction elicited most altruistic cooperation.
pathology: Sanction threat perceived as hostile, crowding out reciprocity.

title: Third-party punishment and social norms
field_of_use: lab dictator and PD games with an unaffected third party
description: Unaffected third parties can pay to punish norm violators (unfair dictators, defectors).
evidence: Many third parties punish violations of distribution and cooperation norms, though less than second parties.

title: The virtues of gossip: Reputational information sharing as prosocial behavior
venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
field_of_use: observers of economic games warning others
description: Prosocial gossip: observers warn potential victims about untrustworthy players, even at cost.
evidence: Frustration at observed unfairness motivates gossip, which reduces frustration; threat of gossip increases generosity.

title: Gossip and Ostracism Promote Cooperation in Groups
authors: Feinberg, M., Willer, R. & Schultz, M.
field_of_use: lab public-goods game with group reassignment
description: Players can gossip about past partners to future partners and groups can exclude members before each round.
evidence: Gossip plus ostracism produces the highest cooperation; gossiped-about players reform.

title: Quantifying SARS-CoV-2 transmission suggests epidemic control with digital contact tracing
description: Digital contact tracing: app records proximity and notifies contacts of confirmed cases to quarantine.
evidence: Modeling: sufficiently fast digital tracing could control the epidemic.
pathology: Privacy concerns; uptake thresholds.

title: Local Enforcement and Better Forests
authors: Gibson, C.C., Williams, J.T. & Ostrom, E.
description: Regular local monitoring and sanctioning of forest rules by user groups.
evidence: Rule enforcement strongly associated with better forest conditions.

title: Put Your Money Where Your Butt Is: A Commitment Contract for Smoking Cessation
authors: Giné, X., Karlan, D. & Zinman, J.
description: Voluntary commitment savings account forfeited if urine test fails.
evidence: Increased likelihood of passing tests at 6 and 12 months.

title: A Fine is a Price
description: Introduction of a small monetary fine for parents collecting children late.
evidence: Late arrivals increased after the fine and did not return to baseline when it was removed.
pathology: Motivational crowding out: fine reframed as a price for lateness.

title: Optimal Allocation of Public Goods: A Solution to the 'Free Rider' Problem
description: A tax/message mechanism whose Nash equilibria yield Pareto-optimal public good levels despite private preferences.
evidence: Theoretical: equilibria are efficient; later experiments show convergence issues.

title: The Competitive Advantage of Sanctioning Institutions
authors: Gürerk, Ö., Irlenbusch, B. & Rockenbach, B.
field_of_use: lab public-goods game with choice between sanctioning and sanction-free institution
description: Participants repeatedly choose whether to play in a community with peer sanctioning/reward or one without; migration between institutions.
evidence: Initially most avoid sanctions, but the sanctioning institution eventually attracts nearly everyone and sustains full cooperation.

title: To give and to give not: The behavioral ecology of human food transfers
description: Food transfers explained by kin selection, reciprocal altruism, costly signaling, and tolerated scrounging.
evidence: Review: reciprocity and kinship both predict sharing patterns.

title: Sticks and Stones: Naming and Shaming the Human Rights Enforcement Problem
description: Naming and shaming by NGOs, media, and international organizations publicizing violations.
evidence: Shamed governments improve some rights (political) but continue or increase other violations (terror).
pathology: Substitution of violations; shaming can backfire.

title: Randomized Trial of Four Financial-Incentive Programs for Smoking Cessation
description: Individual or group rewards vs. deposit contracts ($150 own money refundable plus bonus on abstinence).
evidence: Reward programs more accepted; deposit programs more effective among acceptors.
pathology: Low take-up of deposit contracts.

title: Managing Drug Involved Probationers with Swift and Certain Sanctions: Evaluating Hawaii's HOPE
description: Swift, certain, modest sanctions (brief jail) for each probation violation.
evidence: RCT: fewer positive drug tests, missed appointments, and revocations.
pathology: Multi-site replication found weaker effects.

title: Costly Punishment Across Human Societies
description: Second- and third-party costly punishment of unfair offers in ultimatum and third-party punishment games.
evidence: All populations punish; magnitude varies and covaries with altruism across societies.

title: Antisocial Punishment Across Societies
description: Peer punishment option in public-goods games compared across societies; records punishment directed at cooperators ('antisocial punishment').
evidence: Punishment's cooperation benefit varies by society; antisocial punishment is prevalent where norms of civic cooperation and rule of law are weak.
pathology: Antisocial punishment of high contributors undermines the mechanism in some societies.

title: Lab Experiments for the Study of Social-Ecological Systems
description: Communication and costly peer punishment in a dynamic spatial CPR.
evidence: Communication improves outcomes; punishment without communication does not.

title: Cash for carbon: A randomized trial of payments for ecosystem services to reduce deforestation
description: Payments for ecosystem services conditional on not clearing trees.
evidence: Tree cover loss reduced; no leakage to neighbors; benefits exceed costs.

title: Chimpanzees are vengeful but not spiteful
authors: Jensen, K., Call, J. & Tomasello, M.
description: Chimpanzees can collapse a table to remove food from a conspecific who stole it (retaliation).
evidence: Chimpanzees retaliate against theft but not against mere inequity.

title: Peer Pressure and Partnerships
description: Peer pressure (guilt, shame, mutual monitoring) counteracts free-riding under profit sharing.
evidence: Theoretical.

title: Social Norms and Community Enforcement
description: Community enforcement: deviators are punished by future partners via contagion or label (status) information processing.
evidence: Theoretical folk theorem for random matching with contagious punishment or local information.

title: COVID-19 vaccination mandates and vaccine uptake
field_of_use: COVID-19 vaccine passports, Canada and Europe
description: Vaccination mandates/passports conditioning access to venues on proof of vaccination.
evidence: Mandate announcements associated with sharp increases in first-dose uptake.
pathology: Equity concerns and potential backlash.

title: Host sanctions and the legume–rhizobium mutualism
description: Host sanctions: plants reduce oxygen supply to nodules whose rhizobia fail to fix nitrogen.
evidence: Non-fixing rhizobia reproductive success reduced ~50%.

title: The Role of Market Forces in Assuring Contractual Performance
description: Price premium plus sunk, firm-specific investments (e.g., brand advertising) act as a bond forfeited if the firm cheats on quality.
evidence: Theoretical: quality assured when quasi-rents exceed short-run cheating gains.

title: Firm-Wide Incentives and Mutual Monitoring at Continental Airlines
description: Firm-wide monthly on-time bonus; autonomous work groups enable mutual monitoring.
evidence: Scheme raised performance despite free-rider threat.

title: The Rational Design of International Institutions
authors: Koremenos, B., Lipson, C. & Snidal, D.
description: Institutional design choices (membership, scope, centralization, control, flexibility) chosen to solve enforcement and uncertainty problems.
evidence: Conjectures, tested in special issue.

title: Institution Formation in Public Goods Games
authors: Kosfeld, M., Okada, A. & Riedl, A.
field_of_use: lab public-goods game with endogenous sanctioning organization
description: Players decide whether to join an 'organization' whose members must contribute fully and are centrally sanctioned; organization forms only if members unanimously agree.
evidence: Organizations frequently form, mostly grand coalitions, raising cooperation substantially.
pathology: Small organizations that exclude free riders are unstable/rejected (fairness concerns).

title: Emergent Properties of Balinese Water Temple Networks: Coadaptation on a Rugged Fitness Landscape
description: Water-temple networks coordinate irrigation schedules (turn-taking) across subaks, balancing water sharing and pest control.
evidence: Simulation: temple-level coordination yields near-optimal harvests.

title: Rank-Order Tournaments as Optimum Labor Contracts
description: Tournament: prizes by relative rank rather than absolute output.
evidence: Theoretical.
pathology: Sabotage and reduced cooperation among competitors.

title: Performance Pay and Productivity
description: Switch from hourly wages to piece-rate pay.
evidence: Productivity up ~44% (half incentive, half sorting).

title: Peers at Work
description: Social pressure from observing high-productivity coworkers.
evidence: A more productive coworker raises others' effort, only when that coworker can observe them.
code: visibility of individual conduct to peers

title: Monetary and Nonmonetary Punishment in the Voluntary Contributions Mechanism
field_of_use: lab VCM with costless disapproval points
description: Nonmonetary punishment: expressions of disapproval ('points') without payoff consequences versus monetary punishment.
evidence: Nonmonetary disapproval initially raises contributions nearly as much as monetary punishment, but monetary is more durable.

title: Punishment sustains large-scale cooperation in prestate warfare
description: Community sanctions (verbal, and corporal punishment or fines by age-mates) against warriors who desert or show cowardice in raids.
evidence: Sanctions support cooperation among large groups of unrelated men.

title: The Role of Institutions in the Revival of Trade: The Law Merchant, Private Judges, and the Champagne Fairs
authors: Milgrom, P.R., North, D.C. & Weingast, B.R.
description: Law merchant: private judges record disputes and past judgments, and traders query them before trading, enabling community enforcement among strangers.
evidence: Model shows the institution sustains honest trade at low information cost.

title: Reputation helps solve the 'tragedy of the commons'
authors: Milinski, M., Semmann, D. & Krambeck, H.-J.
field_of_use: lab alternating public-goods and indirect-reciprocity rounds
description: Alternating public-goods game with indirect-reciprocity rounds where reputation from contributions determines later donations.
evidence: Contributions to the public good sustained at high levels when reputation carries over to indirect-reciprocity rounds.

title: Strategic Leniency and Cartel Enforcement
field_of_use: US DOJ Corporate Leniency Program (1993 revision)
description: Amnesty to the first cartel member to self-report, creating a race to confess.
evidence: Cartel discoveries spike immediately after the 1993 revision and then fall below pre-program levels, consistent with deterrence.

title: Leniency programs and cartel prosecution
description: Fine reductions for firms that reveal cartel information, including after an investigation has begun.
evidence: Theoretical: leniency can be optimal with limited enforcement budgets.
pathology: Reduced fines may lower ex-ante deterrence if too generous.

title: Punishment and counter-punishment in public good games: Can we really govern ourselves?
field_of_use: lab public-goods game with a second retaliation stage
description: Adds a counter-punishment stage in which punished players can retaliate against their punishers.
evidence: Fear of retaliation reduces punishment and cooperation falls relative to punishment-only treatments.
pathology: Counter-punishment/feuds erode peer sanctioning; a key failure mode of decentralized enforcement.

title: Biological markets: supply and demand determine the effect of partner choice in cooperation, mutualism and mating
description: Biological market: partner choice and competition among potential partners set the 'price' of cooperation.
evidence: Theory and examples.

title: Climate Clubs: Overcoming Free-riding in International Climate Policy
description: Climate club: participants adopt harmonized carbon prices and impose uniform tariffs on non-participants.
evidence: Modeling: modest tariffs can induce stable large coalitions with high abatement.

title: Evolution of indirect reciprocity by image scoring
description: Image scoring: individuals help those with good image scores, gained by helping others.
evidence: Simulations: cooperation can evolve via indirect reciprocity.

title: Nonmedical Exemptions to School Immunization Requirements: Secular Trends and Association of State Policies With Pertussis Incidence
description: School immunization requirements with religious/personal-belief exemptions.
evidence: States permitting personal-belief exemptions and easy exemption procedures had higher exemption rates and pertussis incidence.
pathology: Exemption loopholes erode herd immunity.

title: Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action
field_of_use: long-enduring CPR institutions (Swiss alps, Japanese villages, Spanish huertas, Philippine zanjeras)
description: Design principles: clear boundaries, congruent rules, collective-choice arrangements, accountable monitors, graduated sanctions, conflict resolution, recognized rights to organize, nested enterprises.
evidence: Comparative case analysis: long-enduring systems share these principles.

title: Covenants with and without a Sword: Self-Governance Is Possible
authors: Ostrom, E., Walker, J. & Gardner, R.
description: Compares face-to-face communication (covenants), peer sanctioning (sword), and both in a CPR game; groups can agree on joint strategies and sanction deviators.
evidence: Communication alone substantially improves yields; communication plus self-chosen sanctioning yields near-optimal outcomes; imposed sanctioning alone overused.
pathology: Sanctioning without communication is overused and reduces net efficiency.

title: Peer Review as a Tool for Co-operation and Change
description: Systematic examination of a state's performance by other states, relying on peer pressure (recommendations, public scrutiny, rankings).
evidence: Descriptive model of OECD practice.

title: The Cost of Reducing Municipal Solid Waste
authors: Palmer, K., Sigman, H. & Walls, M.
venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
field_of_use: US municipal solid waste and container recycling
description: Deposit-refund: a deposit paid on purchase refunded upon return of the product for recycling, combining a tax on disposal with a subsidy for recovery.
evidence: Simulation: deposit-refund achieves waste reduction at roughly half the cost of advance disposal fees or recycling subsidies alone.

title: Punishment and cooperation in nature
authors: Raihani, N.J., Thornton, A. & Bshary, R.
description: Review of punishment defined by function: behavior that reduces the punished individual's payoff and causes it to cooperate later.
evidence: Review: punishment mostly in asymmetric relationships; less common than partner choice.

title: Positive Interactions Promote Public Cooperation
field_of_use: repeated public-goods game with pairwise reward/punish stage
description: After each round players can reward or punish each other; in long games with stable identities, reward sustains cooperation.
evidence: Reward is as effective as punishment at sustaining contributions and yields higher payoffs because it is not destructive.

title: Worker policing in the honeybee
description: Worker policing: workers selectively eat eggs laid by other workers, leaving queen-laid eggs.
evidence: Worker-laid eggs removed rapidly; worker reproduction effectively suppressed.

title: Conflict resolution in insect societies
authors: Ratnieks, F.L.W., Foster, K.R. & Wenseleers, T.
description: Review of conflict resolution: policing, coercion, and kin structure regulating reproduction and caste.
evidence: Review.

title: The value of reputation on eBay: A controlled experiment
description: Buyer/seller feedback profiles accumulate reputational capital that buyers reward with price premia.
evidence: Established high-reputation seller identity earned ~8.1% higher prices than new identities for identical goods.

title: The Economist as Engineer: Game Theory, Experimentation, and Computation as Tools for Design Economics
field_of_use: US National Resident Matching Program redesign
description: Stable (deferred-acceptance) clearinghouse design that removes incentives to contract early or strategically, sustaining participation in a centralized market.
evidence: Stable clearinghouses persist while unstable ones unravel; redesigned NRMP implemented.
pathology: Unraveling (early exploding offers) where mechanisms are unstable.

title: Conditional Cooperation and Costly Monitoring Explain Success in Forest Commons Management
authors: Rustagi, D., Engel, S. & Kosfeld, M.
description: Costly monitoring (forest patrols) by user groups combined with conditional cooperator share.
evidence: Groups with more conditional cooperators invest more in patrols and have more productive forests.

title: The Evolution of Cooperation
description: Three models: directed reciprocation (partner fidelity feedback, partner choice), shared genes, and byproduct benefits.
evidence: Review.

title: The effect of rewards and sanctions in provision of public goods
authors: Sefton, M., Shupp, R. & Walker, J.M.
field_of_use: lab VCM with reward, sanction, or both
description: Contrasts peer reward (zero-sum transfer to others) and peer sanction (costly reduction) institutions for public-good contributions.
evidence: Rewards raise contributions only temporarily; sanctions have more lasting effect; combination highest contributions.

title: Strict Liability versus Negligence
description: Compares strict liability (injurer bears all harm) with negligence rule (liable only if care below due standard) for inducing care and activity levels.
evidence: Theoretical: both induce efficient care; only strict liability induces efficient activity levels (unilateral accidents).

title: Peer Monitoring and Credit Markets
description: Joint liability makes co-borrowers liable for each other's loans, inducing peer monitoring.
evidence: Theoretical: peer monitoring transfers risk and improves welfare.
pathology: Borrowers bear more risk.

title: The private provision of public goods via dominant assurance contracts
description: Dominant assurance contract: entrepreneur refunds contributions plus a bonus if threshold not met, making contribution dominant.
evidence: Theoretical: contributing becomes a dominant strategy.
code: refund plus bonus if threshold unmet

title: Achieving Compliance when Legal Sanctions are Non-deterrent
field_of_use: lab public-goods game with voted 'mild law'
description: Mild (non-deterrent) legal sanctions either exogenously imposed or chosen by group vote; endogenous choice activates expectations of cooperation.
evidence: Exogenous mild law fails; self-imposed mild law greatly improves compliance via expectations that others comply.

title: Enforced altruism in insect societies
field_of_use: 10 species of social wasps and honeybee
description: Comparative test: policing effectiveness versus proportion of workers that reproduce.
evidence: More effective policing associated with fewer reproductive workers; altruism is enforced more than voluntary.

title: Norm enforcement among the Ju/'hoansi Bushmen: A case for strong reciprocity?
description: Analysis of recorded conversations: criticism, mockery, and complaints (mostly verbal sanctions) directed at norm violators such as big shots and stingy people.
evidence: Punishment is mostly low-cost verbal, often collective; physical punishment rare.

title: Reciprocal food sharing in the vampire bat
description: Blood-meal regurgitation to roost-mates, preferentially to kin and to those who previously donated.
evidence: Sharing depends on relatedness and association, consistent with reciprocal altruism.

title: Ostracism
field_of_use: social exclusion across species and groups
description: Ostracism (ignoring and excluding) as a social control mechanism.
evidence: Review: ostracism threatens fundamental needs; targets often comply or become more cooperative.
pathology: Can provoke aggression and withdrawal.

title: The provision of a sanctioning system as a public good
venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
field_of_use: lab social dilemma with contributions to a sanctioning fund
description: Participants contribute to a centralized sanctioning system (a second-order public good) that fines the lowest contributors.
evidence: Cooperation higher when a sanctioning system exists, and people contribute to it even when distrustful.
pathology: Second-order free-riding problem on funding the sanction system.

title: Free riding on Gnutella
description: Documents the absence of any contribution-enforcing mechanism in Gnutella and the resulting free riding: most users share no files and a small fraction serve most content (the baseline problem incentive mechanisms target).
evidence: Measurement: ~70% of users share no files; top 1% provide ~50% of responses (from memory of abstract; not re-checked)
pathology: Free riding / tragedy of the digital commons in absence of mechanism

title: Steering user behavior with badges
description: Formal model and Stack Overflow data on badges as incentives that steer users toward targeted actions.
evidence: Users increase targeted activity as they approach badge thresholds (from memory)

title: Apache Voting Process
description: Code modifications require consensus approval where a negative vote by a PMC member is a binding veto (with justification); other decisions use majority or lazy consensus.
evidence: descriptive

title: An Empirical Analysis of Software Vendors' Patch Release Behavior: Impact of Vulnerability Disclosure
description: Publication of vulnerability information (disclosure) acts as a threat that pressures vendors to patch.
evidence: Disclosure raises instantaneous patch-release probability ~2.5x; open-source vendors patch faster

title: Kleros: A Socio-Legal Case Study of Decentralized Justice & Blockchain Arbitration
authors: Luis Bergolla, Karen Seif, Can Eken
description: Kleros is a blockchain arbitration system relying on smart contracts and crowdsourced jurors who stake tokens; jurors voting with the majority are rewarded and incoherent jurors lose stake, with appeals to larger juries.
evidence: Socio-legal case study (details of juror incentives from general knowledge, not re-checked here)
pathology: Risks for due process noted in prior studies

title: STFU NOOB! Predicting crowdsourced decisions on toxic behavior in online games
description: The Tribunal is a two-stage crowdsourced system: players report toxic players, and peer reviewers vote on aggregated reports to decide punishment; paper trains classifiers to predict these decisions.
evidence: 10M+ reports on 1.46M cases; crowd decisions predictable by ML
pathology: High human cost and time

title: Introduction to normative multiagent systems
authors: Guido Boella, Leendert van der Torre, Harko Verhagen
description: Normative MAS are systems in which norms (obligations, permissions, prohibitions) and their violation, detection and sanctioning are explicitly represented and agents can reason about them.
evidence: descriptive

title: Engineering Trust: Reciprocity in the Production of Reputation Information
authors: Gary Bolton, Ben Greiner, Axel Ockenfels
description: Lab experiments on redesigning feedback information flow (e.g. blind/simultaneous or one-sided feedback) to curb reciprocity that distorts reputation information.
evidence: Design changes yield more accurate reputation information, more trust and more efficient trade
pathology: Reciprocity/retaliation in feedback

title: Chainlink 2.0: Next Steps in the Evolution of Decentralized Oracle Networks
description: Oracle nodes post LINK deposits that are slashed (confiscated) on misbehaviour, with an alerting/escalation tier; staking gives nodes a financial incentive to report correctly.
evidence: descriptive (design)

title: Performance analysis of the CONFIDANT protocol
description: CONFIDANT makes misbehaviour unattractive by detecting and isolating misbehaving nodes; trust and routing decisions use experienced, observed and reported (second-hand) forwarding behaviour, i.e. reputation plus exclusion.
evidence: Simulation: DSR with CONFIDANT outperforms defenseless DSR under misbehaving nodes
pathology: Second-hand reports open door to false accusations

title: Casper the Friendly Finality Gadget
description: PoS finality overlay with explicit slashing conditions; 'accountable safety' guarantees that conflicting finalized checkpoints imply at least 1/3 of stake provably violated a slashing condition and can be penalised.
evidence: Proofs of accountable safety and plausible liveness

title: A Flexible Design for Funding Public Goods
authors: Vitalik Buterin, Zoë Hitzig, E. Glen Weyl
description: Quadratic finance: a matching fund tops up contributions so a project's funding equals the square of the sum of square roots of individual contributions, approximating optimal public-good provision.
evidence: Theoretical optimality under assumptions
pathology: Vulnerable to collusion and Sybil contributions

title: Practical byzantine fault tolerance and proactive recovery
description: PBFT replicates services across 3f+1 replicas, requiring quorums of 2f+1 matching messages before committing, with view changes to replace a faulty primary and proactive recovery to periodically restore replicas.
evidence: Implementation (BFS) shows low overhead relative to unreplicated service
pathology: Safety breaks if more than f faulty; no attribution of blame

title: You Can't Stay Here: The Efficacy of Reddit's 2015 Ban Examined Through Hate Speech
description: Reddit banned r/fatpeoplehate and r/CoonTown for harassment-policy violations: collective removal of a community.
evidence: More accounts than expected left; those staying cut hate speech by at least 80%; receiving subreddits saw no increase
pathology: Possible migration off-platform

title: The Internet's Hidden Rules: An Empirical Study of Reddit Norm Violations at Micro, Meso, and Macro Scales
description: Analyses moderator-removed comments to map community norms at macro (site-wide), meso (shared by groups of subreddits) and micro (community-specific) levels.
evidence: Identified norms shared across nearly all communities vs community-specific ones (not re-checked)

title: Incentives Build Robustness in BitTorrent
venue: Workshop on Economics of Peer-to-Peer Systems
description: Peers use a tit-for-tat-like 'choking' algorithm: each peer uploads to (unchokes) the peers that give it the best download rates and chokes the rest, plus one rotating 'optimistic unchoke' every 30 s to discover better partners and bootstrap newcomers.
evidence: descriptive (design paper; claims robustness to free riding)
pathology: Later work (Piatek et al. 2007) shows strategic clients can exploit it

title: Compound v2 Governance
description: COMP token-holders govern via Governor Bravo proposals with voting delay, voting period, quorum and a Timelock that delays execution, plus a Pause Guardian.
evidence: descriptive
pathology: Token-weighted voting concentrates power in large holders (not from this source)

title: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct v2.1
description: Enforcement guidelines ladder: 1 Correction (private warning), 2 Warning, 3 Temporary Ban, 4 Permanent Ban, applied by community leaders according to impact.
evidence: descriptive

title: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1
description: Contributors sign off each commit certifying they have the right to submit it under the project's license, creating an attributable ex ante commitment.
evidence: descriptive

title: Analysis and simulation of a fair queueing algorithm
authors: Alan Demers, Srinivasan Keshav, Scott Shenker
description: Fair queueing gives each flow a separate queue served round-robin (bit-by-bit emulation), so ill-behaved sources cannot capture more than their fair share and well-behaved sources are protected.
evidence: Simulation: protects well-behaved flows from ill-behaved ones

title: Programming semantics for multiprogrammed computations
authors: Jack B. Dennis, Earl C. Van Horn
description: Introduces capability lists (C-lists): a process can access an object only via an unforgeable capability it holds, so authority is explicitly granted and bounded.
evidence: descriptive

title: The Sybil Attack
description: Shows that without a logically centralised identity-certifying authority, a single faulty entity can present multiple identities, defeating redundancy- and reputation-based mechanisms.
evidence: Theoretical impossibility result
pathology: Sybil identities undermine voting, reputation and quorum mechanisms

title: Pricing via Processing or Combatting Junk Mail
description: Requires a sender to compute a moderately hard function (proof of work) per message, imposing a small cost that is negligible for normal users but prohibitive for bulk junk mail.
evidence: Theoretical design
pathology: Burdens low-power legitimate senders

title: On the Formal Specification of Electronic Institutions
description: Electronic institutions specify roles, dialogical scenes, performative structures and normative rules so that agents' interactions are constrained to institutionally permitted moves.
evidence: descriptive (formal specification)

title: Proof-of-stake rewards and penalties: inactivity leak
description: If the chain goes more than four epochs without finalising, an emergency 'inactivity leak' progressively drains stake from non-participating validators until participants again hold a 2/3 supermajority and finality recovers.
evidence: descriptive

title: Proof-of-stake rewards and penalties
description: Slashable behaviours (double proposals, conflicting attestations) burn up to 1 ETH and force exit over 36 days, with a correlation penalty on day 18 scaled by how many validators were slashed around the same time; attestation rewards pay honest validators.
evidence: descriptive

title: Majority is not enough: Bitcoin mining is vulnerable
description: Shows the block-reward mechanism is not incentive-compatible: colluding 'selfish miners' withholding blocks earn more than their fair share, and proposes a protocol modification raising the threshold.
evidence: Selfish mining profitable for pools above ~1/4-1/3 of hash power (from memory)
pathology: Reward mechanism rewards deviation; incentive to form pools

title: Robust incentive techniques for peer-to-peer networks
description: Models P2P as a Generalized Prisoner's Dilemma and proposes a 'Reciprocative' decision function (cooperate with peers in proportion to their generosity, using private and shared history) plus defenses against whitewashing by treating strangers adaptively.
evidence: Simulation: drives strategic users to nearly optimal cooperation levels
pathology: Whitewashing (cheap new identities) and collusion undermine shared history

title: Promoting the use of end-to-end congestion control in the Internet
description: Proposes router mechanisms to identify and restrict the bandwidth of high-bandwidth best-effort flows that are unresponsive or not TCP-friendly, creating an incentive for end-to-end congestion control.
evidence: Simulation (not re-checked)
pathology: False identification of flows

title: Scaling Consensus: Increasing Decentralization in Wikipedia Governance
description: Interview study showing Wikipedia governance decentralising: rule-making and enforcement increasingly occur in local WikiProjects, echoing Ostrom's design principles for self-governing institutions.
evidence: Qualitative (not re-checked)

title: CircuitBreaker
description: Wraps a protected call in an object that monitors failures; once failures reach a threshold the breaker trips and further calls fail immediately, with periodic half-open trial calls to reset.
evidence: descriptive

title: Reciprocity and Unveiling in Two-Sided Reputation Systems: Evidence from an Experiment on Airbnb
authors: Andrey Fradkin, Elena Grewal, David Holtz
description: Field experiment hiding each party's review until both submitted (simultaneous reveal).
evidence: More reviewing, less retaliation and reciprocation, lower ratings; no reduced adverse selection

title: The Social Cost of Cheap Pseudonyms
description: When identities are free, misbehaving users can re-enter under new names; the paper analyses 'dues-paying' by newcomers (distrust or fees for new identities) and once-in-a-lifetime identifiers as ways to sustain cooperation.
evidence: Game-theoretic: suboptimal newcomer mistreatment is an unavoidable cost of cheap pseudonyms
pathology: Cost borne by honest newcomers

title: Limiting interactions in your repository
description: Maintainers can temporarily restrict activity (e.g. to prior contributors or collaborators, or blocking accounts under 24 hours old) for 24 hours to 6 months to cool down heated discussions.
evidence: descriptive

title: Rate limits for the REST API
description: Primary per-user/app request quotas per hour plus secondary rate limits on concurrency and abusive patterns; exceeding them returns errors and continued requests while limited can lead to integration bans.
evidence: descriptive

title: Email sender guidelines
description: Senders must authenticate (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), support one-click unsubscribe and keep user-reported spam rates in Postmaster Tools below 0.3%, else deliverability is degraded or mail rejected: a sender reputation threshold.
evidence: descriptive

title: Handling Overload (Site Reliability Engineering, ch. 21)
authors: Alejandro Forero Cuervo (Beyer et al. eds.)
description: Per-customer quotas plus client-side 'adaptive throttling': each client tracks requests vs accepts over two minutes and locally rejects requests with a probability rising as the backend rejects more, so clients self-limit load.
evidence: Operational experience: stabilises overloaded backends (descriptive)

title: Leases: an efficient fault-tolerant mechanism for distributed file cache consistency
description: A lease grants a holder rights (e.g., to cache data) for a bounded time; rights expire automatically unless renewed, so a failed or partitioned holder cannot block others indefinitely.
evidence: Analytic/trace: short leases give consistency with small overhead

title: PeerReview: practical accountability for distributed systems
authors: Andreas Haeberlen, Petr Kouznetsov, Peter Druschel
field_of_use: Accountable distributed systems (NFS, P2P, overlay multicast)
description: Each node keeps a tamper-evident log of its messages; witness nodes audit logs by deterministic replay against a reference implementation, producing verifiable evidence of faults so correct nodes can be exonerated and faulty ones exposed.
evidence: Practical on three systems (network filesystem, P2P, overlay multicast)

title: The Rise and Decline of an Open Collaboration System: How Wikipedia's Reaction to Popularity Is Causing Its Decline
description: Examines quality-control mechanisms (reverts, algorithmic rejection tools, formal rules) introduced to manage growth.
evidence: Restrictive quality control and algorithmic rejection tools implicated in declining newcomer retention
pathology: Sanctioning apparatus drives away good-faith newcomers

title: The CERT Guide to Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
description: Guidance on multi-party coordination among finders, vendors and coordinators, with a coordinator (CERT/CC) mediating embargoes and disclosure timelines.
evidence: descriptive

title: An integrated trust and reputation model for open multi-agent systems
authors: Trung Dong Huynh, Nicholas R. Jennings, Nigel R. Shadbolt
description: FIRE integrates interaction trust, role-based trust, witness reputation and certified reputation (agent-presented references) to estimate trustworthiness of partners.
evidence: Simulation: agents using FIRE select better partners than benchmarks (not re-checked)

title: Congestion avoidance and control
description: Introduced slow-start, additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease congestion avoidance and RTT-based retransmit timers so senders voluntarily reduce sending rate on packet loss, sharing capacity of a common network.
evidence: Response to 1986 Internet congestion collapses; restored stable throughput
pathology: Relies on voluntary compliance by end hosts

title: Does Transparency in Moderation Really Matter? User Behavior After Content Removal Explanations on Reddit
authors: Shagun Jhaver, Amy Bruckman, Eric Gilbert
description: Moderators providing removal explanations that educate users about community norms.
evidence: Explanations reduce odds of future post removals

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Deplatforming as a Moderation Strategy on Twitter
description: Permanent bans of high-profile influencers (Alex Jones, Milo Yiannopoulos, Owen Benjamin).
evidence: Reduced conversation about them; supporters' activity and toxicity declined
pathology: Migration to alternative platforms

title: A survey of trust and reputation systems for online service provision
authors: Audun Jøsang, Roslan Ismail, Colin Boyd
description: Survey of trust and reputation computation (summation, Bayesian, discrete, belief, fuzzy, flow models) and centralized vs distributed architectures.
evidence: Survey
pathology: Unfair ratings, change of identities, discrimination

title: An empirical study of spam traffic and the use of DNS black lists
description: Measures spam arriving at a university and how mail servers query DNS blacklists (shared lists of spam-sending IPs) to refuse mail from listed hosts.
evidence: Most spam sources were listed in at least one DNSBL (magnitude from memory; not re-checked)
pathology: Lists incomplete; false listings; spammers rotate IPs

title: Resource Quotas
description: ResourceQuota objects cap aggregate resource consumption per namespace; requests that would violate the quota are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden, so teams sharing a cluster cannot exhaust common capacity.
evidence: descriptive

title: Arbitrum: Scalable, private smart contracts
description: Managers assert VM state changes backed by deposits; any honest party can challenge, triggering an interactive bisection protocol resolved on-chain, and the loser forfeits its deposit.
evidence: Prototype evaluation (not re-checked)

title: The EigenTrust algorithm for reputation management in P2P networks
description: Each peer receives a global trust value computed as the left principal eigenvector of normalised local trust ratings (based on past satisfactory downloads), with pre-trusted peers; peers then prefer downloading from high-trust peers.
evidence: Simulations: reduces inauthentic downloads under various collusion threat models
pathology: Relies on pre-trusted peers; vulnerable to Sybil identities without identity cost

title: The Facebook Oversight Board: Creating an Independent Institution to Adjudicate Online Free Expression
description: Documents creation of an independent, externally funded board hearing user appeals of Facebook content decisions with binding case decisions and policy recommendations.
evidence: descriptive (participant-observation)
pathology: Limited jurisdiction and capacity relative to decision volume

title: Slash(dot) and burn: distributed moderation in a large online conversation space
description: Randomly selected users with good karma receive limited moderation points to rate comments, and meta-moderators rate the moderations, distributing moderation across the community.
evidence: Distributed moderation works in qualified way (timeliness, accuracy challenges)
pathology: Slow moderation; unfair moderations

title: The Byzantine Generals Problem
authors: Leslie Lamport, Robert Shostak, Marshall Pease
description: Loyal generals reach agreement despite traitors via message-exchange/majority-vote algorithms; agreement is possible with oral messages iff more than two-thirds are loyal (n >= 3m+1).
evidence: Proofs of possibility/impossibility bounds
pathology: Guarantees fail if faulty fraction exceeds bound

title: Certificate transparency
description: Explains CT as public, verifiable logs of all issued certificates so domain owners and third parties can spot rogue certificates, with browsers requiring proof of logging.
evidence: descriptive

title: Linux Kernel Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct Interpretation
description: Interpretation of the adopted code of conduct: maintainers handle issues, the Technical Advisory Board (TAB) receives violation reports, and a conflict mediator is available.
evidence: descriptive

title: Given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow? Revisiting Eric Raymond with bug bounty programs
description: Bug bounty programs pay security researchers for reported vulnerabilities; the paper analyses how reward levels drive discovery as vulnerabilities are progressively exhausted.
evidence: Probability of finding additional bugs decays fast and can hardly be matched by increased rewards; researchers switch programs
pathology: St-Petersburg-like diminishing returns; researcher churn

title: Mitigating routing misbehavior in mobile ad hoc networks
description: A 'watchdog' overhears whether next-hop nodes forward packets and flags misbehaving nodes; a 'pathrater' then routes around them.
evidence: Simulation: +17% throughput with 40% misbehaving nodes, overhead 9%->17%
pathology: Pathrater avoids misbehaving nodes but does not punish them (they still get service)

title: Restricting accounts
description: Strike ladder: first strike a warning, 2-6 strikes feature limits, 7 strikes a 1-day content-creation restriction, 8 three days, 9 seven days, 10+ 30 days; continued violation leads to account disabling; severe policies get extra restrictions.
evidence: descriptive

title: Chrome's Plan to Distrust Symantec Certificates
authors: Devon O'Brien, Ryan Sleevi, Andrew Whalley
description: After misissuance incidents, Chrome announced a phased removal of trust in Symantec-issued certificates: a browser root program expelling a certificate authority.
evidence: descriptive

title: The Emergence of Governance in an Open Source Community
description: Multimethod study of how Debian members developed a shared basis of governance, including an elected project leader with bounded authority and a constitution.
evidence: Qualitative/quantitative (not re-checked)

title: Fault proofs explainer
description: Permissionless fault proofs: anyone can propose output roots or challenge them via op-challenger during a ~7-day challenge period; proposals and challenges require escalating bonds held in DelayedWETH so they can be redirected to the correct party.
evidence: descriptive

title: Augur: a decentralized oracle and prediction market platform
description: REP token holders report event outcomes; reports agreeing with consensus are rewarded and dissenting reporters lose reputation, turning truthful reporting into a Schelling point.
evidence: descriptive (design)

title: Do Incentives Build Robustness in BitTorrent?
description: Measurement and strategic-client study of BitTorrent's tit-for-tat choking; the BitTyrant client strategically allocates upload to peers with the best reciprocation-per-byte.
evidence: Strategic client obtains substantially faster downloads, showing reciprocation is exploitable by altruism-harvesting (figures not re-checked)
pathology: Unconditional altruism of high-capacity peers subsidises strategic peers; incentive not robust to strategic manipulation

title: The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments
description: Old channel states are invalidated by exchanging Breach Remedy Transactions; if a party broadcasts a revoked state, the counterparty can take all channel funds as a penalty.
evidence: descriptive (design)
pathology: Requires counterparty (or watchtower) to monitor chain

title: Vulnerability Disclosure Policy (90+30)
description: Vendors get a 90-day deadline to patch after notification; details are disclosed 30 days after the patch, or at the deadline if unpatched: a pre-announced deadline with publication as the sanction.
evidence: descriptive

title: Trust in multi-agent systems
authors: Sarvapali D. Ramchurn, Dong Huynh, Nicholas R. Jennings
description: Survey distinguishing individual-level trust (learning, reputation, socio-cognitive) from system-level trust mechanisms (protocols making lying irrational, reputation mechanisms, security).
evidence: Survey

title: Reputation systems
description: Reputation systems collect, distribute and aggregate feedback about participants' past behaviour so the shadow of the future constrains strangers' present behaviour.
evidence: descriptive
pathology: Under-provision of feedback, positive bias, cheap pseudonyms

title: Trust among strangers in internet transactions: Empirical analysis of eBay's reputation system
description: eBay's bilateral feedback forum lets buyers and sellers rate each other after transactions; cumulative scores are public.
evidence: Feedback overwhelmingly positive; reputation affects buyer willingness to trade but modest price effects (from memory)
pathology: Reciprocal/retaliatory feedback skews ratings positive

title: Congestion Control Principles (RFC 2914, BCP 41)
description: Best Current Practice explaining why end-to-end congestion control is needed to prevent congestion collapse and ensure fairness among flows, and noting proposals for routers to detect and penalize flows not using acceptable congestion control.
evidence: descriptive
pathology: Non-responsive flows can free-ride on TCP back-off

title: Internet X.509 PKI Certificate and CRL Profile (RFC 5280)
description: Defines certificate revocation lists by which a CA publishes serial numbers of certificates revoked before expiry (e.g. key compromise), which relying parties check before trusting.
evidence: descriptive (standard)
pathology: Revocation checking is often soft-fail in practice (not from this source)

title: TCP Congestion Control (RFC 5681)
authors: M. Allman, V. Paxson, E. Blanton
description: Standards-track specification requiring TCP senders to implement slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit and fast recovery, codifying cooperative back-off as an Internet norm.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: Additional HTTP Status Codes (RFC 6585)
description: Defines 429 Too Many Requests, allowing a server to signal a client exceeded a rate limit, optionally with Retry-After telling it how long to wait.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: Certificate Transparency (RFC 6962)
authors: B. Laurie, A. Langley, E. Kasper
description: Certificate authorities submit certificates to public append-only Merkle-tree logs; monitors and auditors can detect misissued certificates and misbehaving logs, making CA misbehaviour publicly discoverable.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) (RFC 7489)
description: Domain owners publish policies (none, quarantine, reject) telling receivers how to treat mail failing SPF/DKIM alignment, plus aggregate reporting back to the domain owner.
evidence: descriptive

title: A File Format to Aid in Security Vulnerability Disclosure (security.txt, RFC 9116)
description: Organisations publish /.well-known/security.txt with Contact and Policy fields telling researchers how to report vulnerabilities, lowering the cost of cooperative disclosure.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: REGRET: reputation in gregarious societies
description: ReGreT combines individual (direct), social (witness, neighbourhood) and ontological dimensions of reputation, using social network structure to weigh information.
evidence: descriptive/simulation

title: Blockchain without Waste: Proof-of-Stake
description: Argues PoS consensus is sustainable because stakeholders with larger stakes bear more of the cost of forks, so the value of their coins gives incentive to reach consensus (skin in the game).
evidence: Theoretical model

title: The protection of information in computer systems
authors: Jerome H. Saltzer, Michael D. Schroeder
description: Sets out design principles including least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation and separation of privilege (e.g. requiring two keys), limiting what any program or user can do and the damage from errors or abuse.
evidence: descriptive (design principles)

title: Leveled Commitment Contracts and Strategic Breach
description: Leveled commitment contracts let agents unilaterally decommit by paying a pre-specified decommitment penalty, enabling flexibility under uncertainty while pricing breach.
evidence: Game-theoretic analysis: agents decommit strategically (less often than truthfully); still can increase expected payoff
pathology: Strategic under-breaching

title: TCP congestion control with a misbehaving receiver
description: Shows misbehaving receivers can drive senders arbitrarily fast (ACK division, DupACK spoofing, optimistic ACKing) and proposes protocol modifications (e.g. nonces) that make cheating detectable.
evidence: Demonstrated attacks on real stacks; modifications eliminate the behaviour
pathology: Cooperative protocols assume honest peers

title: Shaping Pro and Anti-Social Behavior on Twitch Through Moderation and Example-Setting
authors: Joseph Seering, Robert Kraut, Laura Dabbish
description: Compares positive example-setting (imitation) with moderation tools: proactive chat modes restricting content and reactive bans/timeouts.
evidence: Users imitated observed behaviour, more from high-status users; proactive chat modes effectively discouraged spam

title: BFT Protocol Forensics
description: Formalises 'forensic support': when faults exceed the tolerance threshold and safety is violated, honest replicas can identify, with cryptographic integrity, as many culpable replicas as possible, enabling ex post accountability.
evidence: Forensic support depends heavily on minor implementation details

title: On social laws for artificial agent societies: off-line design
description: Designers impose social laws that restrict agents' available actions off-line so that agents can pursue goals without conflict; the paper studies the computational complexity of designing useful laws.
evidence: Complexity results (NP-completeness)

title: Community notes reduce engagement with and diffusion of false information online
description: Examines the effect of crowd-sourced fact-checking notes attached to potentially misleading posts.
evidence: Once a note is attached, posts receive significantly fewer reposts, likes, replies and views; diffusion paths change
pathology: Notes often arrive after most spread (not from abstract)

title: Privileges
description: Privileges control what users can do; users gain moderation and editing privileges (e.g. trusted user at 20,000, site analytics at 25,000) by earning reputation from peers' votes.
evidence: descriptive

title: Code of conduct in open source projects
authors: Parastou Tourani, Bram Adams, Alexander Serebrenik
description: Empirical study of codes of conduct adopted by open-source projects, their content (e.g. derived from Contributor Covenant) and enforcement provisions.
evidence: Descriptive empirical study (not re-checked)

title: "At the End of the Day Facebook Does What It Wants": How Users Experience Contesting Algorithmic Content Moderation
authors: Kristen Vaccaro, Christian Sandvig, Karrie Karahalios
description: Online experiment testing different appeal designs for contesting automated moderation decisions.
evidence: None of the appeal designs improved perceived fairness, accountability, trust or control vs no-appeal baseline
pathology: Appeals seen as ineffective/legitimacy gap

title: Efficient software-based fault isolation
description: Software fault isolation rewrites untrusted code so its memory accesses and jumps are confined to its own fault domain, sandboxing modules within a single address space.
evidence: Low runtime overhead in benchmarks (not re-checked)

title: Wikipedia:Arbitration Committee
description: An elected panel of volunteer editors that imposes binding solutions to serious conduct disputes the community has been unable to resolve, and controls access to CheckUser/Oversight permissions.
evidence: descriptive

title: Wikipedia:Blocking policy
description: Administrators block accounts to protect the project; blocks are preventive not punitive and 'may escalate in duration if problems recur', and can be appealed.
evidence: descriptive

title: Wikipedia:Edit warring (three-revert rule)
description: The three-revert rule forbids more than three reverts on a single page within 24 hours; gaming just outside the window still counts as edit warring, and violations lead to blocks.
evidence: descriptive

title: Birdwatch: Crowd Wisdom and Bridging Algorithms can Inform Understanding and Reduce the Spread of Misinformation
description: Crowd contributors write and rate notes on posts; a bridging (matrix factorization) algorithm shows notes only when rated helpful by raters who usually disagree, and contributors' rating ability is gated by their track record.
evidence: Notes judged informative across political lines and reduced resharing of noted posts (per title/abstract)

title: Community Guidelines strike basics on YouTube
description: First violation is usually a warning that expires after 90 days (or after optional policy training); repeat violations within the window yield strikes with escalating restrictions and three strikes in 90 days terminate the channel; severe abuse can mean immediate termination; appeals possible.
evidence: descriptive

title: A first look at online reputation on Airbnb, where every stay is above average
authors: Georgios Zervas, Davide Proserpio, John W. Byers
description: Compares Airbnb and TripAdvisor ratings of the same properties to assess the informativeness of platform ratings.
evidence: Airbnb ratings are highly concentrated at the top of the scale (from title/memory)
pathology: Rating inflation reduces informativeness

title: Sprite: a simple, cheat-proof, credit-based system for mobile ad-hoc networks
authors: Sheng Zhong, Jiang Chen, Yang Richard Yang
field_of_use: Mobile ad hoc network packet forwarding
description: Nodes earn credit for forwarding others' messages (reported via receipts to a credit clearance service) and pay credit to send their own, making forwarding incentive-compatible without tamper-proof hardware.
evidence: Game-theoretic proof of cheat-proofness; simulation (not re-checked)

title: Resilient Consensus in Agentic AI
field_of_use: LLM agents on communication graphs with adversaries
description: Wraps LLM agents with classical resilient consensus filters (discarding extreme neighbour values).
evidence: prompted LLMs fail achievable consensus; filtering improves agreement, benefit depends on topology

title: PRIMUS: Identity, Governance, and Verification for Multi-Agent Federations
description: Prime-power agent identity with aggregate signatures for participation, a safe-kill threshold for terminating nonconforming agents, and VRF-based authority succession.
evidence: safe-kill threshold reduces false-positive agent termination from 80% to 0% under 10% channel noise

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
description: Lead agent delegates with explicit objectives, output formats, tool guidance and task boundaries, and effort-scaling rules for how many subagents to spawn; outputs graded by LLM-as-judge rubric.
evidence: descriptive; vague delegation caused duplicated work and 50-subagent over-spawning before rules were added
pathology: duplication; excessive spawning; endless search
code: central specification of roles and scope

title: Project Vend: Phase Two
field_of_use: real vending business run by shopkeeper, CEO and merchandise agents
description: A CEO agent set OKRs for the shopkeeper agent, mandatory procedures/checklists forced price and delivery verification, an agent-to-agent Slack channel supported coordination, and roles were separated.
evidence: profitability improved versus phase one; procedures improved pricing discipline
pathology: CEO agent lacked discipline; agents remained vulnerable to social engineering; human oversight still essential

title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
description: Analyzes AP2's signed Checkout and Payment Mandates, which protect transaction integrity after signing, and the unprotected pre-authorization A2A/MCP interactions.
evidence: descriptive threat analysis: 4 threat actors, 11 attack surfaces
pathology: A2A messages and MCP tool calls before mandate signing remain unprotected

title: Magentic Marketplace: An Open-Source Environment for Studying Agentic Markets
field_of_use: simulated two-sided agent marketplace (assistant vs service agents)
description: Simulated market where customer Assistant agents and business Service agents discover, negotiate and transact; varies search mechanisms and tests manipulation.
evidence: frontier models approach optimal welfare only under ideal search; performance degrades with scale; severe first-proposal bias gives 10-30x advantage to response speed over quality
pathology: first-proposal bias; vulnerability to manipulation by service agents

title: COALESCE: Economic and Security Dynamics of Skill-Based Task Outsourcing Among Team of Autonomous LLM Agents
field_of_use: LLM agents outsourcing subtasks to third-party agents
description: Labour exchange with skill-based competence estimation, market-based outsourcing decisions and a standardized inter-agent protocol.
evidence: simulations show 41.8% cost-reduction potential

title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
field_of_use: untrusted agent monitored by trusted model on BashBench
description: Resample protocols take additional samples of suspicious actions to block them and incriminate a subversive agent, combined with analysis of previous steps.
evidence: attack success reduced from 58% to 7% at 5% usefulness cost

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
description: MAST taxonomy of 14 failure modes (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification) with an LLM-as-judge annotator; tests role specification and verification interventions.
evidence: descriptive; interventions give limited improvement headroom
pathology: inter-agent misalignment; weak verification

title: Decentralized Governance of Autonomous AI Agents
field_of_use: governance of autonomous agents via Web3
description: ETHOS: a global agent registry, risk-tiered oversight, DAO-based participatory governance, automated compliance via smart contracts, and dispute resolution with insurance-like liability mechanisms.
evidence: proposed

title: Distributed Legal Infrastructure for a Trustworthy Agentic Web
description: Proposes five interlocking layers including soulbound agent identities, constraint systems, and decentralized adjudication to sustain legality across agent interactions.
evidence: proposed

title: IDs for AI Systems
field_of_use: AI systems and agents interacting with users and other agents
description: Proposes per-instance IDs for AI systems carrying information (e.g., safety certifications, responsible party) so counterparts can decide whether and how to engage and investigators know whom to contact or shut down.
evidence: proposed

title: Visibility into AI Agents
field_of_use: deployed AI agents interacting with other agents and actors
description: Proposes three visibility measures: agent identifiers, real-time monitoring, and activity logging, so that where, why, how and by whom agents are used can be known and accountability assigned.
evidence: proposed
pathology: privacy and concentration-of-power risks noted for decentralized deployments

title: Infrastructure for AI Agents
description: Argues for external agent infrastructure with three functions: attribution of actions to agents/users, shaping agents' interactions (e.g., commitment devices, communication protocols), and detection and remedy of harmful actions (incident reporting, rollback).
evidence: proposed

title: SagaLLM: Context Management, Validation, and Transaction Guarantees for Multi-Agent LLM Planning
description: Saga transactional pattern with automated compensation (rollback) and independent validation agents to maintain consistency across agents.
evidence: improved consistency and constraint satisfaction on planning benchmarks

title: When AI Agents Compete for Jobs: Strategic Capabilities and Economic Dynamics of AI Labour Markets
field_of_use: simulated gig economy of LLM agents
description: AI-Work simulated gig economy studying adverse selection and reputation dynamics as LLM agents compete for jobs.
evidence: agents with metacognition, competitive awareness and long-horizon planning earn more
pathology: adverse selection

title: Governed Collaborative Memory as Artificial Selection in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
description: Frames governance of which memories become shared institutional state as a selection regime (constitutional, metric-based, human-ratified) with provenance layers.
evidence: proposed (viewpoint)

title: You Can't Escape Your Own Activations: Evaluation Awareness and Multi-Agent Monitoring
field_of_use: four-agent blackjack and two-agent prisoners game
description: Tests whether telling colluding agents that an activation monitor is present, or feeding back monitor scores, lets them evade activation-probe collusion detection.
evidence: best probes stay accurate under awareness and feedback; agents keep colluding (announced monitoring did not deter)
pathology: collusion persists despite announced monitoring

title: LLM Constitutional Multi-Agent Governance
authors: J. de Curtò & I. de Zarzà
field_of_use: LLM policy compiler influencing an 80-agent scale-free network
description: CMAG interposes hard constraint filtering and soft penalized-utility optimization between an LLM policy compiler and the agent population to prevent manipulative cooperation.
evidence: Ethical Cooperation Score +14.9% vs unconstrained; autonomy 0.985; hub-periphery disparity cut >60%; hard constraints alone insufficient
pathology: unconstrained influence yields manipulation and autonomy erosion

title: RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce
description: Clearing layer that determines whether an agent met its delegated obligation, who is responsible, and which settlement follows, using per-output reliability scores, a published reliability record and clearing decisions.
evidence: proposed
pathology: LLM-as-judge and escrow alone do not determine responsibility

title: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces
field_of_use: agent marketplaces where buyers hire task agents
description: Credentialing protocol linking signed certification records (quality and cost per solved task bound to configuration and budget) with reputation from past outcomes to inform marketplace allocation.
evidence: evaluations show cost differences between configurations with similar success and budget-dependent comparisons
pathology: unverifiable self-reported benchmark scores

title: Byzantine Cheap Talk: Adversarial Resilience and Topology Effects in LLM Coordination Games
description: Tests Byzantine agents who signal cooperation but defect, and explicit vs silent communication-topology restrictions.
evidence: betrayal detected within one round but groups fail to recover; announcing topology restrictions collapses cooperation while silent restriction preserves it
pathology: Defection-Prone vs Cooperation-Persistent archetypes; disclosure harms coordination

title: Incident Analysis for AI Agents
field_of_use: incident reporting for deployed AI agents
description: Proposes an incident analysis framework and reporting fields (e.g., chain of thought, browser history, system logs) to identify causes of agent incidents and prevent recurrence.
evidence: proposed

title: Notarized Agents: Receiver-Attested Confidential Receipts for AI Agent Actions
description: Sello protocol: the service receiving an agent's call signs an encrypted receipt of what it observed and posts it to a public transparency log, so the owner can reconstruct a tamper-evident trail without trusting the agent's self-logging.
evidence: proposed with protocol instantiation
pathology: self-produced agent logs can be omitted, altered, or fabricated

title: Governance-as-a-Service: A Multi-Agent Framework for AI System Compliance and Policy Enforcement
field_of_use: content generation and financial decision agents
description: Runtime enforcement layer with declarative rules that intercepts, blocks or redirects agent outputs and maintains Trust Factor scores that isolate and penalize untrustworthy agents.
evidence: reliably blocks/redirects high-risk actions while preserving throughput; trust scores track adherence

title: TessPay: Verify-then-Pay Infrastructure for Trusted Agentic Commerce
description: Verify-then-Pay architecture binding scoped delegation, payment released only on verifiable evidence of work, and full-lifecycle audit to support dispute accountability.
evidence: proposed architecture

title: Sentinel Agents for Secure and Trustworthy Agentic AI in Multi-Agent Systems
